contract:
agenthub Phases 2 and 3 wire contract. Frozen at Step 0 and changed only by the integrator. Normative prose is in DESIGN-phase2-3.md sections 1.1-1.10 and 6.3. The code below is verbatim and type-checks under TypeScript 6.0.3 strict (verified in scratchpad/design/work-final/tc). The contract vectors pass.

=== A. Git conventions (section 1.1) ===
P = land.refPrefix (default refs/agenthub/).
Remote refs:
- refs/heads/<trunk>: only the active lander writes it, by CAS push.
- P land/<full sha>: pushed plainly by the adapter's land and never forced. Deleted atomically with the trunk push, or by GC 1 h after any other terminal state.
- P cand/<epoch8>/<L-id>/<sha12>: the staged candidate, pushed plainly by the lander under a new name. Staged before `pushing`, when parked for approval, and on check failure. Deleted after landing, or 7 days after another terminal state.
Ref names come from landRef() and candidateRef() in @agenthub/contract.
Local refs: refs/agenthub/backup/<branch>/<ms> in agent worktrees (written by sync, pruned after 14 days). The lander mirror uses refs/remotes/origin/<trunk>, refs/agenthub/land/*, refs/agenthub/cand/* and refs/agenthub/admit-trunk.
Trailers, last paragraph of every lander commit: Agenthub-Landing: <project>/<L-id>; Agenthub-Hub: <hub epoch uuid>; Agenthub-Source: <full sha of the landed commit>; Agenthub-Attempt; Agenthub-Task; Agenthub-Agent; Agenthub-Resolved: clean | structural <paths> | ai:<model> <paths>; Agenthub-Checked: <12 hex of sha256(check cmd)>; Agenthub-Approved: <kind>:<human> (only when approvals were needed). Agent-written text passes through sanitizeMessageText, which strips TRAILER_LINE_RE lines. Subject: '<task title or summary line> (L-n)'. The body lists the squashed commits (at most 20). The author is copied from the landed commit; the committer is the lander identity.
Identity: a first-parent trunk commit IS landing L only if Landing == <project>/<L.id> AND Hub == the hub epoch AND Source == L.commit. Searches run over first-parent commits from L.first_base (exclusive) to the tip.
Landed base: landedBase(T, X). B = merge-base(T, X). S* = the newest Agenthub-Source on T's first-parent history (depth 500, any epoch) that is an ancestor of X. Base = S* if S* exists and is not an ancestor of B, else B.
Squash only: one candidate C per landing. C = commit-tree(merged tree, parent T0), and C^1 == T0 is asserted.

=== B. Config (section 1.2) ===
agenthub.json (the lander reads trunk's copy at T0; the adapter prefers refs/remotes/<remote>/<trunk>:agenthub.json and falls back to the worktree's).
- land: remote (origin), trunk (main), check (required), checkTimeoutMin (20, 1-240), checkEnv {NAME: string}, allowDirtyTree (false), protected (glob | {paths, approvers?, distinct?})[], approval {distinct: true, timeoutHours: 24}, refPrefix (refs/agenthub/), structural (auto|off), resolver {enabled false, model claude-opus-5-5, maxFiles 4, maxFileBytes 65536, exclude [**/.env*, **/*.pem, **/*.key, **/secrets/**], requireApproval false}, claimGate (fail|warn), keepPlaceRetries (2), sendbackGraceMin (30), maxFiles (2000), externalPushes (warn|pause), holdTurn (false).
- sync: {auto: true, staleEdit: warn|off}.
- symbols: {enabled: true, exclude: [], maxSymbolsPerEdit: 12}.
ALWAYS_PROTECTED = [agenthub.json, .gitattributes]. They are always the first rule.
Parse with parseTeamSections(value, {strict}). Strict: the lander, the land tool, doctor; the first problem throws, unknown keys included. Lenient: hooks, digest, guard; never throws, falls back to defaults and reports problems. Without a land section (or, in lenient mode, without a check), there is no queue and land runs in Phase 1 record mode.
The lander reports LandPolicy (claim_gate, keep_place_retries, sendback_grace_min, approval_timeout_hours) in POST /lander/trunk, and the hub applies it.
hub-server flags:
- --lander-token / HUB_LANDER_TOKEN. Header x-hub-lander-token is required for lander routes and reserved-key claims. Without the flag, those routes work only on loopback; on a network address they answer 403 lander_token_required.
- --approvers FILE / HUB_APPROVERS_FILE. JSON {name: 'sha256:<hex>'}. Without it, approvals answer 403 approvals_disabled.
- --allow-unauthenticated-approvals. Refused unless bound to loopback.
Lander-local config: <workdir>/lander.json (0600 enforced), flags and env. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY comes from env only; it is read into memory, then deleted from process.env.

=== C. Storage (section 1.3) ===
claims gains landing_id TEXT and mapper TEXT.
landings gains: updated_at, queue_seq, phase, phase_at, attempt, lander, lease_claim_id, in_doubt, deadline_at, base_sha, first_base, trunk_base, candidate, candidate_ref, candidate_checked, trunk_sha, files, scope, mapper, protected, approval, hold_ids, report, failure, retries, retry_of, retry, supersedes, superseded_by, waits_for, landed_with, reconciled, started_at, ended_at. Index: UNIQUE (project) WHERE status='running'.
New tables:
- landing_approvals: append-only, enforced by triggers.
- lander_control(project, paused, trunk, policy).
- symbol_changes, with a unique in_progress row per (agent, file, symbol).
Store: transaction(fn, {durable}) sets synchronous=FULL around BEGIN IMMEDIATE, used for landing and control writes. projectsWithDueWork(now) replaces projectsWithDueClaims.

=== D. Landing transitions (section 1.4) ===
T0 record mode: 409 landing_queue_active once the project ever had a claim on LANDER_LEASE_KEY.
T1 POST /land {queue:true} -> submitted.
- Guards: full sha (bad_commit); task owner/closed/blocked rules; a predecessor in pushing -> too_late; the advisory gate (409 claim_conflict with details.conflicts; nothing is created).
- Replay per (agent, commit).
- Supersede of a live same-(agent, task) predecessor: its holds move, its queue_seq is inherited.
- Retry chain: the latest failed landing within 24 h gives retry_of, and queue_seq is inherited while retry <= keep_place_retries.
- Holds = advisory scope plus the entries of the claims the Phase 1 rule selects. Those claims end with 'moved to landing L-n'.
- Task -> landing.
T2 admit -> queued: holds made exact (gate), approval = required minus approvals carried over from the chain with the same kind and digest.
T3 admit -> failed: not_pushed, nothing_to_land, too_large, claim_conflict, contains_unlanded.
T4 next -> running/merging: fenced, no running landing, not paused, lowest queue_seq whose waits_for is terminal. attempt+1, lander, lease_claim_id, deadline 10 min.
T5 advance phase change (merging -> resolving -> checking -> pushing). Entering pushing needs candidate, candidate_ref, tree, trunk_base and required, and every requirement must be granted (409 approval_missing). The write is durable, and deadline_at is null.
T6 running (not pushing) -> needs_approval: checks passed on the candidate, which is staged; candidate_checked = true; the slot is freed.
T7 approve, in submitted, queued, running or needs_approval: authenticated, the digest equals a pending requirement's (approval_stale), the rule's approvers and distinct (not_approver). Appends a landing_approvals row. A needs_approval landing with nothing left pending -> queued, keeping queue_seq.
T8 needs_approval -> failed: approval_rejected, or approval_timeout past deadline_at.
T9 running (not pushing) -> queued: trunk_moved, lander_stopping, remote_unavailable, config_invalid or trunk_rewritten from the lander; lander_lost on lease end; step_timeout past the deadline. Limits: trunk_moved 3 (then failed trunk_busy), lander_lost 3 (then failed lander_lost), step_timeout 2 (then failed lander_stuck). queue_seq is kept.
T10 running/pushing on lease end -> in_doubt = true. The slot stays occupied, and next returns it with resolve: true.
T11 running -> landed: advance {landed}, or resolve {landed}.
T12 pushing -> queued: resolve {requeue}, only when trunk moved past trunk_base without the candidate, or the staged candidate is gone.
T13 running (not pushing) -> failed.
T14 cancel: author or approver, any live state except pushing (409 too_late).
T15 superseded, inside T1.
T16 reconcile inside POST /lander/trunk: any non-landed landing whose identity matches a reported trunk commit -> landed, reconciled = true.
Landed effects: holds released via endClaim with 'landed L-n', then promoteQueued; task -> done and announceUnblocked; also_landed get landed_with; symbol_changes recorded; control.trunk updated; events landing.landed and trunk.moved.
Failure effects: holds -> leases (landing_id null, expires_at = now + max(ttl, sendback_grace)); task -> in_progress; event landing.failed; a direct message from the lander.
Approval kinds, each with a digest from gitops.approvalDigest:
- protected: (path, base blob, head blob), computed at admission.
- merged: (path, T0 blob, C blob), when trunk also changed a protected path.
- ai_resolution: (path, base, ours, theirs, result), when resolver.requireApproval.
Each rule is satisfied by an approval with the same digest from a human it allows; distinct means the approver is not humanOf(landing.agent). A protected approval carries over within a retry or supersede chain while its digest is unchanged.

=== E. Lander lease and fencing (section 1.5) ===
The lease is a Phase 1 claim on LANDER_LEASE_KEY (.git/agenthub/lander): exclusive, queue:true, ttl 60 s, sent with x-hub-lander-token. Reserved-key claims need lander credentials and exactly [LANDER_LEASE_KEY]. One agent id per process: lander/<host>-<pid>-<4hex>. Standbys hold queued claims and are promoted by promoteQueued.
Every lander write carries lease {lease_claim_id, epoch}. Inside write(), after expireDue, the hub needs an active claim with that id on the key, held by the caller, and epoch == store.epoch(); else 409 not_lander. advance also needs status running, the same attempt and the same lease_claim_id; else 409 landing_stale. A request already reflected in the row returns replayed: true.
endClaim on the lease key applies T9 (lander_lost), or T10 for a landing in pushing.
The lander heartbeats every 15 s. It never starts advance{pushing} or the trunk push unless its last ack is younger than ttl/3.

=== F. Holds (section 1.6) ===
A hold is a claim with holder = agent, landing_id = L and expires_at = HOLD_EXPIRES; at most one exclusive and one shared per landing.
- renewLeases uses expires_at = max(expires_at, now + ttl). Holds stay in the heartbeat's renewed count, so the feed accounting is unchanged.
- claim() coverage excludes holds: a hold never covers its holder's new request, which gets a separate lease.
- release of a hold -> 409 held_by_landing; all, task_id and files skip holds.
- Wait-graph node for a hold = landing:<id>, so holds cause no false deadlocks.
- check() counts other agents' holds.
- toConflict fills scope and landing_id.
setHolds:
- Mode: an entry is shared if the agent's own claim on it was shared, or if others hold overlapping claims and all of them are shared (the auto rule); else exclusive.
- Gate: exclusive vs anything, or shared vs exclusive, is a conflict. gate=fail applies nothing; gate=warn leaves the conflicting entries out of the hold.

=== G. Routes (section 1.7), all under /v1/p/:project ===
Agent routes:
- POST /land (LandRequest -> LandResult).
- GET /landings?status=&agent=&task=&limit= and GET /landings/stats?days= (LandingStats). Both are registered before /landings/:id.
- GET /landings/:id.
- POST /landings/:id/cancel (author or approver).
- POST /claims and POST /claims/check (CheckRequest).
- POST /claims/release (held_by_landing).
- POST /symbol-changes and GET /symbol-changes?since_ms=&status=.
- GET /lander -> {lease: LanderInfo|null, control}.
Approver routes (headers x-hub-approver and x-hub-approver-token):
- POST /landings/:id/approve (ApproveRequest), POST /landings/:id/reject (RejectRequest).
- POST /lander/resume (LanderResumeRequest).
Lander routes (header x-hub-lander-token):
- POST /lander/next (LanderNextRequest -> LanderNextResult).
- POST /landings/:id/admit (LandingAdmitRequest -> LandingAdmitResult).
- POST /landings/:id/advance (LandingAdvanceRequest -> LandingAdvanceResult).
- POST /landings/:id/resolve (LandingResolveRequest -> LandingAdvanceResult).
- POST /lander/trunk (TrunkReportRequest -> {control}).
- POST /lander/pause (LanderPauseRequest -> {control}).
Unchanged Phase 1 routes: heartbeat, status (gains queue, lander, control), events, WS feed. Error bodies may carry details.

=== H. Events (section 1.8; no agent free text; targets null) ===
- landing.created {landing_id, agent, task_id, commit, position, supersedes, retry_of}
- landing.updated {landing_id, agent, task_id, status, phase, attempt, reason (admitted|picked|phase|requeued:<code>|in_doubt|approved|cancelled|superseded), position}
- landing.needs_approval {landing_id, agent, task_id, kinds, paths<=20, approvers, parked}
- landing.landed {landing_id, agent, task_id, trunk_sha, files<=200, resolved_by, also_landed, reconciled}
- landing.failed {landing_id, agent, task_id, code, files<=50}
- trunk.moved {from, to, landing_id|null, files<=200, foreign}
- lander.paused and lander.resumed {reason, by}
- symbol.changed {change_id, agent, file, symbol, name, kind, status, landing_id, task_id}
Claim event data gains landing_id and scope. Record mode keeps emitting land.requested.

=== I. Error codes (section 1.9) ===
- 400: bad_commit, invalid_symbol.
- 409: landing_queue_active, claim_conflict (details.conflicts), task_landing, too_late, landing_closed, held_by_landing, not_lander, landing_stale, approval_missing (details.missing), approval_stale.
- 403: lander_token_required, approvals_disabled, not_approver.

=== J. Symbol scope (section 1.10) ===
Keys: Name, Container.member, Container, default, @imports, @toplevel. They must match SYMBOL_KEY_RE (at most 200 characters).
Overlap rules:
- different files never overlap;
- a whole-file entry overlaps everything in its file;
- @imports never overlaps @imports;
- otherwise entries overlap when equal or one is a dot-prefix of the other.
Mapper gating: symbol entries count only between claims with the same non-null mapper; otherwise everything compares at file level.
Edit mapping with changedSymbols(path, before, after):
- the claim covers changed, added and removed keys, keys moved outside the LCS of the key sequences, and keys holding contained errors;
- whitespace-only gap changes belong to no key, except that an edit changing only whitespace claims @toplevel;
- uncontained parse errors, more than 12 keys per edit (40 per file in a landing diff), Write, NotebookEdit, new, deleted, binary, too-large and unsupported files, and an unverified grammar all fall back to file-level.
MAPPER_VERSION = 'sym1;vtsw0.3.1;wts0.27.0;' + the first 8 hex of the grammar manifest's sha256.

=== K. Fixed names (section 6.3.6) ===
hub-lander init|run [--once]|doctor|resolve-anthropic; exit codes 0 and 2. Test env, honoured only with NODE_ENV=test: AGENTHUB_LANDER_FAULTS, AGENTHUB_RESOLVER_STUB.
hub land|landings [--stats]|landing|cancel|approve|reject|sync [--merge] [--recover]|uses|lander [resume --accept-trunk]|doctor|guard --pre-push.
MCP tools: land, landing_status, land_cancel, hub_sync, hub_wait (+landing_id), who_uses, impacts, claim (path#Symbol).
Worktree files under the git dir G: agenthub/sync.lock, agenthub/sync.json, agenthub/inflight/<session>~<tool_use_id>, agenthub/held/<landing>, agenthub/mergebase, agenthub/impacts-acked.json. Common dir: agenthub/refcache/<blob>.<mapper8>.json.
Fault points: after-admit, after-next, during-merge, during-checks, after-checks, after-candidate-staged, after-pushing-ack, after-trunk-push, before-landed-ack, after-landed-ack.
Contract fixtures: packages/hub/test/fixtures/contract/*.json, one per request and response, listed in section 6.3.7.

=== M. packages/hub/src/protocol.ts: appended after the Phase 1 declarations (verbatim) ===
// ===================================================================== Phase 2: landing queue
// Appended after the Phase 1 declarations. Every sha in a new field is a full
// lowercase object id (FULL_SHA_RE in @agenthub/contract); Phase 1 `recorded`
// rows may hold a 12-character commit.

export type LandingStatus =
  /** Phase 1 record-only rows; never processed. */
  | 'recorded'
  /** Created by `land`; holds taken from the agent's advisory scope; waits for lander admission. */
  | 'submitted'
  /** Admitted; waits for its turn (queue order: queue_seq). */
  | 'queued'
  /** Waits for a human approval; outside the one running slot. */
  | 'needs_approval'
  /** The one landing per project the lander works on (see `phase`). */
  | 'running'
  | 'landed'
  | 'failed'
  | 'cancelled'
  | 'superseded';

/**
 * Phases of a running landing. `pushing` is the write-ahead phase: the candidate
 * is staged on the remote and recorded before trunk is updated. A landing in
 * `pushing` can't be cancelled or superseded (409 too_late), is never requeued
 * by time or lease loss (it becomes `in_doubt`), and only a lander that has
 * looked at the remote moves it on.
 */
export type LandingPhase = 'merging' | 'resolving' | 'checking' | 'pushing';

export type LandingFailureCode =
  | 'not_pushed' // the land ref is missing or doesn't point at the commit
  | 'nothing_to_land'
  | 'too_large'
  | 'claim_conflict' // the change touches code another agent holds (claimGate: fail)
  | 'contains_unlanded' // the commit contains another agent's landing that did not land
  | 'conflict' // the merge ladder left conflicts
  | 'resolver_failed' // the AI resolver declined, its output failed verification, or the checks failed on it
  | 'checks_failed'
  | 'check_timeout'
  | 'checks_modified_tree'
  | 'trunk_busy' // trunk moved outside the queue more than 3 times in one landing
  | 'push_rejected' // the remote refused the trunk update for policy reasons (the project pauses)
  | 'approval_rejected'
  | 'approval_timeout'
  | 'lander_lost' // the lander died while running it more than 3 times
  | 'lander_stuck' // a step outlived its deadline more than twice
  | 'lander_error'; // a lander bug or infrastructure failure; not caused by the change

export type RequeueReason =
  | 'trunk_moved'
  | 'lander_lost'
  | 'lander_stopping'
  | 'step_timeout'
  | 'remote_unavailable'
  | 'config_invalid'
  | 'trunk_rewritten'
  | 'approved';

export type ResolvedBy = 'none' | 'clean' | 'structural' | 'ai';

/** What an approval covers (design §1.4): the agent's own protected change, the merged protected content, or an AI resolution. */
export type ApprovalKind = 'protected' | 'merged' | 'ai_resolution';

export interface ApprovalRule {
  /** Globs as written in trunk's agenthub.json. */
  paths: string[];
  /** Humans who may approve; null = any configured approver. */
  approvers: string[] | null;
  /** The approver must not be the landing agent's human. */
  distinct: boolean;
}

/** An approval the landing still needs, as computed by the lander from trunk's config. */
export interface ApprovalRequirement {
  kind: ApprovalKind;
  /** sha256 hex over exactly the content a human is shown (gitops.approvalDigest); `hub approve` recomputes it. */
  digest: string;
  /** Protected paths it covers, sorted. */
  paths: string[];
  /** Every rule must be satisfied by an approval with this digest from someone the rule allows. */
  rules: ApprovalRule[];
  /** merged / ai_resolution: the staged candidate the digest covers, and the trunk tip it was built on. */
  candidate: string | null;
  candidate_ref: string | null;
  trunk_base: string | null;
}

/** A granted approval (append-only audit, table landing_approvals). */
export interface LandingApproval {
  kind: ApprovalKind;
  digest: string;
  /** The approver's human name. */
  by: string;
  at: number;
  /** The approver's words: shown to agents as a teammate's text, never as instructions. */
  note: string;
  /** Set when carried over from an earlier landing of the same chain with the same digest. */
  carried_from: string | null;
}

export interface ConflictHunk {
  /** Lines of the conflict-marked file, 1-based. */
  start_line: number;
  end_line: number;
  /** Phase 3: declarations the hunk lies in; [] when unknown. */
  symbols: string[];
  /** Each side capped at 80 lines / 4 KiB. Code written by agents: untrusted text. */
  base: string;
  trunk: string;
  yours: string;
}

/** A trunk commit since the merge base that changed a conflicted file: who changed the trunk side, and why. */
export interface TrunkChange {
  commit: string;
  /** null: pushed outside the landing queue. */
  landing_id: string | null;
  agent: string | null;
  task_id: string | null;
  /** Another agent's summary: untrusted text. */
  summary: string;
  decisions: Array<{ id: string; summary: string }>;
}

export interface ConflictReport {
  file: string;
  kind: 'content' | 'modify_delete' | 'rename' | 'binary' | 'mode' | 'other';
  /** At most 10 per file. */
  hunks: ConflictHunk[];
  /** Newest first, at most 5. */
  trunk_changes: TrunkChange[];
  tried: ResolvedBy[];
  ai_eligible: boolean;
  /** The resolver's explanation when it declined (untrusted model text). */
  explanation: string | null;
}

export interface CheckReport {
  /** First 12 hex of sha256 of the check command (as in the Agenthub-Checked trailer). */
  command_hash: string;
  exit_code: number | null;
  signal: string | null;
  timed_out: boolean;
  duration_ms: number;
  /** Last 200 lines / 16 KiB, ANSI stripped, secrets redacted. Output of repository code: untrusted text. */
  log_tail: string;
  /** Best effort, from vitest/jest, node:test, mocha, pytest, go test and cargo test output. */
  failed_tests: string[];
  /** true: the trunk tip landed through the queue under the same check command; null: unknown (e.g. a foreign commit). */
  passes_on_trunk: boolean | null;
  /** One shell line that reproduces the run on the agent's machine. */
  reproduce: string;
}

export interface ResolverReport {
  model: string;
  outcome: 'resolved' | 'cannot_resolve' | 'rejected_output' | 'error' | 'skipped';
  files: string[];
  /** Output lines found in none of base/trunk/incoming. */
  novel_lines: number;
  input_tokens: number;
  output_tokens: number;
  /** path → the resolver's explanation (untrusted model text). */
  explanations: Record<string, string>;
}

/** Lander-written report. Only the fields documented as untrusted carry agent- or code-derived text. */
export interface LandingReport {
  /** One paragraph for the author, written by the lander. */
  message: string;
  resolved_by: ResolvedBy | null;
  files_via: Array<{ file: string; via: ResolvedBy }>;
  conflicts: ConflictReport[];
  check: CheckReport | null;
  resolver: ResolverReport | null;
  /** Concrete next steps in order, with exact tool calls and commands. */
  next_steps: string[];
  warnings: string[];
  foreign_commits: string[];
  timings: { queued_ms: number; merge_ms: number; check_ms: number; push_ms: number } | null;
}

/** Superset of the Phase 1 `Landing`; Phase 1 field names are kept (`commit` = the submitted commit). */
export interface Landing {
  id: string;
  project: string;
  agent: string;
  task_id: string | null;
  branch: string | null;
  commit: string | null;
  summary: string;
  status: LandingStatus;
  created_at: number;
  updated_at: number;
  /** Queue order: lower runs first. Kept on requeue; inherited along a retry chain (keepPlaceRetries) and by a superseding landing. */
  queue_seq: number | null;
  /** Computed on read: 1 = next among queued landings (a running one counts as ahead). */
  position: number | null;
  /** Computed on read from recent attempt durations; null without a lander. */
  eta_ms: number | null;
  phase: LandingPhase | null;
  phase_at: number | null;
  /** 0 until a lander first picks it up; +1 per pickup. */
  attempt: number;
  /** The lander process that runs it (lander/<host>-<pid>-<rand>). */
  lander: string | null;
  /** The lander lease claim the current attempt runs under (fencing token, with the hub epoch). */
  lease_claim_id: string | null;
  /** In `pushing` when the lease that ran it ended: the next lease holder must resolve it from the remote first. */
  in_doubt: boolean;
  /** Running (not pushing): the hub requeues it (step_timeout) past this. needs_approval: it fails (approval_timeout) past this. */
  deadline_at: number | null;
  /** The base the lander diffed against (landed base, design §1.1). */
  base_sha: string | null;
  /** The trunk tip of the first attempt: the lower bound of every trailer search for this landing. */
  first_base: string | null;
  /** The trunk tip the current attempt merges onto (T0). */
  trunk_base: string | null;
  /** The staged candidate (set when entering `pushing`, or when parked in needs_approval). */
  candidate: string | null;
  candidate_ref: string | null;

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ scope rules (design §1.10)

/** Two entries of claims made with the same mapper overlap. A missing symbol is the whole file. */
export function entriesOverlap(a: ScopeLike, b: ScopeLike): boolean {
  if (a.file !== b.file) return false;
  if (a.symbol === undefined || b.symbol === undefined) return true;
  if (a.symbol === IMPORTS && b.symbol === IMPORTS) return false;
  return a.symbol === b.symbol || a.symbol.startsWith(`${b.symbol}.`) || b.symbol.startsWith(`${a.symbol}.`);
}

/** A held entry covers a wanted one: a whole-file entry covers the file; a symbol covers itself and its members. */
export function entryCovers(held: ScopeLike, wanted: ScopeLike): boolean {
  if (held.file !== wanted.file) return false;
  if (held.symbol === undefined) return true;
  if (wanted.symbol === undefined) return false;
  return wanted.symbol === held.symbol || wanted.symbol.startsWith(`${held.symbol}.`);
}

/**
 * Mapper gating: symbol entries count only between two claims made with the
 * same non-null mapper. Otherwise each entry is compared as its whole file.
 */
export function comparable(a: ScopedLike, b: ScopedLike): boolean {
  return a.mapper !== null && a.mapper === b.mapper;
}

function fileOnly(e: ScopeLike): ScopeLike {
  return { file: e.file };
}

/** The entries of `b` that some entry of `a` overlaps, with mapper gating. */
export function overlappingEntries<T extends ScopeLike>(a: ScopedLike, b: { scope: T[]; mapper: string | null }): T[] {
  const same = comparable(a, b);
  return b.scope.filter((y) => a.scope.some((x) => (same ? entriesOverlap(x, y) : entriesOverlap(fileOnly(x), fileOnly(y)))));

export function claimCovers(held: ScopedLike, wanted: ScopeLike, wantedMapper: string | null): boolean {
  const same = held.mapper !== null && held.mapper === wantedMapper;
  return held.scope.some((h) => (same ? entryCovers(h, wanted) : h.file === wanted.file && h.symbol === undefined));

// Syntax: '*' = any run without a slash; '**' = any run; '**' followed by a
// slash = zero or more directories; '?' = one character except a slash. The
// glob matches the whole repo path. (Line comments on purpose: a block comment
// would be closed by the double-star-slash in this explanation.)

export function globToRegExp(glob: string): RegExp {
  let re = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < glob.length; i++) {
    const c = glob[i];
    if (c === '*') {
      if (glob[i + 1] === '*') {
        if (glob[i + 2] === '/') {
          re += '(?:.*/)?';
          i += 2;
        } else {
          re += '.*';
          i += 1;

    } else if (c === '?') re += '[^/]';

export function protectedMatches(paths: readonly string[], rules: readonly ProtectedRule[]): Array<{ rule: ProtectedRule; paths: string[] }> {
  const out: Array<{ rule: ProtectedRule; paths: string[] }> = [];
  for (const rule of rules) {

    if (hit.length) out.push({ rule, paths: [...new Set(hit)].sort() });
  }
  return out;
}

decisions: Base design is git-native (highest weighted score); state-machine's safety machinery and agent-experience's agent/human experience are grafted in, and every point where the three drafts disagree is settled in DESIGN section 0.3 (55 rows).
Squash-rebase: every landing becomes one commit whose only parent is the trunk tip it was merged onto, built with git merge-tree in a bare mirror; there is no per-commit rebase mode.

land pushes the full commit sha to refs/agenthub/land/<sha>, a hidden namespace that triggers no CI; land.refPrefix falls back to refs/heads/agenthub/ when the host refuses custom refs, and doctor probes it.
Trunk moves only by git push --atomic --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<trunk>:<T0> <C>:refs/heads/<trunk> :<land ref>, after asserting C^1 == T0, through one unit-tested function, pushTrunk.
At most once is guaranteed by write-ahead: the candidate is staged at refs/agenthub/cand/<epoch8>/<L>/<sha12> and recorded in a durable, fenced pushing phase before trunk moves.

A landing in pushing can't be cancelled, superseded or requeued by time or lease loss; it becomes in_doubt, and the next lease holder resolves it from the remote by pushing the same sha, marking it landed, or requeueing only once the candidate can no longer land.

A commit counts as landing L only if its Agenthub-Landing, Agenthub-Hub (database epoch) and Agenthub-Source trailers all match; searches are bounded below by the landing's first_base, which fixes git-native's collision after a database is recreated.
A lander trunk scan reconciles the hub to git, so any landing found on trunk is marked landed whatever the hub recorded.
The lander lease is an ordinary Phase 1 claim on .git/agenthub/lander held by a per-process id (lander/<host>-<pid>-<rand>), fenced by (lease claim id, hub epoch) inside every write, after expireDue.
Lander routes and reserved-key claims require --lander-token on network-bound hubs and are open only on loopback.
Holds are separate claim rows with landing_id set and expires_at = HOLD_EXPIRES, and renewLeases becomes max(), so heartbeat accounting and the feed are unchanged and no held field is needed.

Holds never cover their holder's new requests, can't be released by the holder, use the wait-graph node landing:<id> so they cause no false deadlocks, and turn back into leases with a 30-minute send-back grace on failure.

Hold scope is the adapter's advisory scope, gated by the hub at land time, then the lander's authoritative diff scope at admission with claimGate fail by default (warn optional), so an unclaimed or mis-mapped edit can't land over another agent's live claim.
The lander admits landings within seconds of land, in a loop that runs alongside the attempt loop: it computes files, symbol scope, protected paths and approval digests, and asks approvers at once.

Protected landings still queue and run their checks; they park in needs_approval only if approval is still missing after the checks pass, and an approved resume on an unchanged trunk pushes the already-checked candidate.

Approvals bind to content digests of three kinds (protected = the agent's change, merged = merged protected content, ai_resolution = the exact blobs); they come from per-human sha256-hashed approver tokens through a TTY-only CLI that recomputes the digest, and the hub refuses pushing without them.
Approvals honour per-rule approvers and a distinct-human rule, a protected approval carries over within a re-land chain while its digest is unchanged, and the audit table is append-only.

Merge attributes are pinned to trunk with --attr-source=<T0>; structural drivers are enabled only in stage 2 via info/attributes and -c, and only paths that conflicted in stage 1 take stage 2's result.

The lander's git never reads global or system config and runs no hooks; checks run in a fresh worktree of the exact candidate with an env allowlist and scratch HOME, and a check that modifies tracked files fails (checks_modified_tree).
There are no automatic check retries and no general check cache; the only reuse is a parked landing's exact checked candidate on an unchanged trunk.

The AI resolver may only rewrite numbered conflict hunks, which are spliced back so every byte outside them is git's merge text; its output passes marker, size, novelty and parse gates and then the checks, and it never sees protected or secret files.

The resolver is a swappable stdin/stdout command; the built-in one calls claude-opus-5-5 through @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.131.0 with streaming, structured output, effort high, adaptive thinking and fallbacks default, and any error degrades to cannot_resolve.

Fix-it send-backs carry conflict hunks with base/trunk/yours and trunk-side attribution (landing, task, decision), failed test names, passes_on_trunk, an exact reproduce command on the staged candidate, and next steps.

Re-lands keep their queue place for 2 retries; land checks locally before pushing (uncommitted and untracked files are refused unless allow_untracked, conflict and protected-path previews); results show position and ETA; hub landings --stats reports the per-chain median land-to-trunk and the first-try rate.

Workspace sync replays commits in the object database and applies them with one git reset --keep, behind a HEAD compare-and-swap, a sync.json write-ahead and a backup ref, and with edit-marker/lock mutual exclusion; it runs only at SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and hub_sync, and never on dirty tracked files.

Stacked landings use landedBase (the newest landed source that is an ancestor of the tip), waits_for a live contained landing, landed_with for the same agent's terminal ones, and contains_unlanded for another agent's.
Phase 1 record-mode land is refused (landing_queue_active) once the project has ever had a lander, and a landing task gets the new status landing.

Phase 3 symbol keys are Name, Container.member, @imports and @toplevel, mapped by diffing outlines of the simulated post-edit text; whitespace-only gaps belong to no key, moves claim their keys, errors contained in one declaration claim it, and anything else falls back to file-level.
Claims carry a MAPPER_VERSION (rule version + pinned grammar versions + manifest hash), and claims made under different versions compare at file level.

Grammars come from @vscode/tree-sitter-wasm 0.3.1 on web-tree-sitter 0.27.0 (no install scripts, verified for 7 languages), with a committed sha256 manifest checked at load; a mismatch makes that language file-level.

Impact warnings need no hub-stored reference index: each agent checks announced signature changes against its own claimed bytes (catching uncommitted callers), who_uses and callers_free use a per-checkout cache keyed by blob sha, and in-progress changes are posted from post-edit.
Shared runtime rules live in a zero-dependency @agenthub/contract and git plumbing in a zero-dependency @agenthub/gitops, so agent machines never install better-sqlite3 or @anthropic-ai/sdk.
Config parsing is strict on the lander, the land tool and doctor, and lenient in hooks, because a config error blocks every edit in Phase 1.
New wire fields are required, and Step 0 makes the listed mechanical edits in hub.ts and sqlite-store.ts so Phase 1 keeps compiling and its tests pass.

Four lanes (H hub, L gitops+lander, A adapter+e2e, S symbols) own disjoint paths; frozen contract files, package.json files and the lockfile belong to nobody and change only at integration checkpoints.
A deterministic port-based protocol simulation with 5 mutation guards, crash tests at 10 fault points, and a two-agent end-to-end suite with a stub resolver are acceptance gates.

Speculative --parallel N pipelining is deliberately left out; the throughput math shows a serial queue meets the 15-minute median up to about 10 landings an hour with 4-minute checks, and pipelining is the first lever if stats show queue wait dominating.

Read DESIGN 2.6 and the frozen resolver-protocol.ts. Build:
(1) Eligibility: content conflicts with all 3 stages, regular text files, not protected, not matching resolver.exclude, at most maxFiles and maxFileBytes, at most 40 hunks, within resolverMaxPerHour.
(2) Input: git merge-file -p --diff3 -L trunk -L base -L incoming over the 3 blobs, with conflict regions numbered 0..n-1. Intents of the incoming landing (task title and description, summary, hold intents, decisions) and of the trunk side (the last 5 trailer-attributed landings touching the file since base). A per-request nonce, redrawn if it appears in any input.
(3) Run the command with stdin/stdout JSON and a 180 s timeout. Env: PATH, a scratch HOME, and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from lander memory for the built-in command only.
(4) Gates, in order: schema valid, status resolved, every hunk id exactly once; no conflict-marker lines unless present in base, ours or theirs; splice the hunk texts into the merged text so the bytes outside the hunks are identical; size limits; novelty (lines in none of base, ours, theirs) at most max(5, 25% of the conflict-region lines); parse (Phase 3, via ResolverPort.parseCheck injected later in L6).
(5) Write the blob with spliceTree; the trailer is ai:<model> <paths>.
(6) With requireApproval, the ai_resolution requirement is approvalDigest over (path, base, ours, theirs, result). On a later attempt with byte-identical stages, reuse the approved result blobs without calling the resolver.
(7) resolve-anthropic: @anthropic-ai/sdk client.beta.messages.stream with model from input, max_tokens 32000, betas server-side-fallback-2026-07-01, fallbacks 'default', output_config {effort: 'high', format: {type: 'json_schema', schema}}, the fixed system prompt (DESIGN 2.6) with cache_control ephemeral, and no thinking parameter. Then finalMessage(). stop_reason refusal or max_tokens gives cannot_resolve; otherwise parse the text and validate with zod. Any API error gives cannot_resolve. Report usage.
(8) The stub modes (AGENTHUB_RESOLVER_STUB): fixture, union, markers, decline, broken, slow. It counts its calls in a file.

risks: Throughput: a serial queue is M/D/1. With 4-minute checks the 15-minute median holds up to about 10 landings an hour (rho about 0.75); at 12 an hour the mean is about 17 minutes. Send-backs add whole cycles per chain. Levers in order: faster checks, fewer send-backs (preflight, sync, stale-base heads-up), then the deliberately omitted speculative --parallel N pipelining.

Trunk safety needs a host rule (a ruleset that lets only the lander identity update trunk and blocks force pushes). Without it, direct pushes are detected (foreign commits, the externalPushes pause option) but not prevented; doctor can't verify the rule.

Custom ref namespaces: refs/agenthub/* depends on the host accepting refs outside refs/heads. doctor probes it; the fallback land.refPrefix refs/heads/agenthub/ makes visible branches that may trigger CI.

Checks run repository code on the lander machine. They can weaken what they check unless check-defining files are protected, and can read the lander user's files unless run as a dedicated OS user or through checkWrapper.

Identity is still self-asserted (a Phase 1 limit). Per-human approver tokens and the lander token raise the bar, but an agent with shell access as the approver's own user can read that user's token file. Per-human authentication is Phase 4.

Structural drivers are unverified here: Mergiraf's driver line comes from its documentation and Weave's CLI is unknown. Both are optional and gated by doctor's self-test; a semantically wrong structural merge is caught only by the checks.
git feature levels: the lander needs merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base and --attr-source (git 2.40 or later), probed by doctor. Agent-side sync falls back to fast-forward-only on older git.

Symbol mapping is heuristic. False negatives surface at the admission claim gate, at the merge or in the checks; false positives (containers, file-level fallbacks, mapper-version mismatches between adapters and the lander) cost parallelism. Upgrade the adapters and the lander together.
Impact warnings are name-based with an import filter: false positives for common member names, and false negatives through dynamic dispatch. They are advisory only.

AI resolver: cost (up to about $0.80 per file at the ceiling, with an hourly cap), latency (up to 3 minutes per file), data egress (opt-in by both the team and the lander operator), and plausible but wrong merges that pass the checks. The pinned SDK 0.131.0's typing of fallbacks with structured outputs must be confirmed in L5; any rejection degrades to cannot_resolve.
Squash history loses per-commit history on trunk (the shas are listed in the commit body) and coarsens git bisect.

The @vscode/tree-sitter-wasm package is VS Code's own distribution. It is pinned and sha256-verified; the fallback is copying the byte-identical wasm files from tree-sitter-* packages installed with --ignore-scripts (Rust needs re-verification).

Holds pin files while a landing waits: parked landings up to approval.timeoutHours, and indefinitely if no lander runs (until a human cancels). Claim-gate failures from stale claims add friction; claimGate warn is the escape hatch.
Dirty worktrees never sync, so agents that never commit before landing see conflicts only at landing (the forecast warns them early).
Restoring an old hub database backup while landers run is unsupported. Trailer identity and the reconcile scan prevent double landings and converge the hub to git.
Event volume grows with landing.*, trunk.moved and symbol.changed events, and there is still no event-log compaction (a Phase 1 limit).

Left out on purpose: speculative pipelining and batching, merge-commit or per-commit history, general check caches and automatic retries, multiple concurrent landers, auto-revert, auto-stash, a hub-stored or LSP reference index, non-code symbol claims, more languages, a default container sandbox, git notes, per-human auth, the dashboard, and a Windows lander.
